Rashi on Pesachim 56a:10:2.hebrew: ה"ג מתירין גמזיות של הקדש של חרוב ושל שקמה - כשהוקדשו הסדנין תחילה וניתוספו הגידולין:
Rashi on Pesachim 56a:10:2.english: This is the reading: They permit consecrated branches of carob and of sycamore - When the trunks were consecrated initially and the [new] growths were added.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:13:1.hebrew: קוצרין לפני העומר ברצון חכמים - כלומר, לא הקפידו חכמים; דאיסורא דאורייתא ליכא, דמקום שאי אתה מביא הוא. ואיסורא דרבנן נמי ליתא — דילמא אתי למיכל מיניה לא גזרו, דהא חדש מיבדל בדילי מיניה כולי שתא, שאינו נוהג אותו כל השנה:
Rashi on Pesachim 56a:13:1.english: They harvest before the omer with the will of the Sages - That is to say, the Sages did not object; for there is no biblical prohibition, since it is a place from which you do not bring [the omer]. And there is no rabbinic prohibition either — [for] they did not decree [a prohibition] lest one come to eat from it, since [people] keep themselves separate from chadash [new grain] all year, as one does not practice [eating] it all year.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:13:2.hebrew: וגודשין שלא ברצון חכמים - כיון דלאו פסידא הוא, גזרו רבנן שימתינו, משום שמתוך שהוא מתעסק בו אתי למיכל מיניה:
Rashi on Pesachim 56a:13:2.english: And they pile [the grain] against the will of the Sages - Since it is not a [case of] loss, the Sages decreed that they should wait, because while one is occupied with it, he might come to eat from it.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:1:1.hebrew: ואוכלין מתחת הנשרין - תחת הדקל המשיר פירותיו היו אוכלין מן הנושרות, וטעמא דכולהו מפרש בגמרא:
Rashi on Pesachim 56a:1:1.english: And they would eat from beneath the shedding [trees] - Beneath the palm tree that sheds its fruit they would eat from the fallen [fruit], and the reason for all of them is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:1:2.english: And they give pe'ah for vegetables - And it is exempt from pe'ah, as explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:1:3.hebrew: ומיחו בידן - משום דקא מפקעי ליה ממעשר, שהיו עניים אוכלים פיאה בטיבלה, דסבורין שהיא פיאה גמורה, ולקט שכחה ופיאה פטורין מן המעשר משום דהפקר נינהו:
Rashi on Pesachim 56a:1:3.english: And they reprimanded them - Because they were removing it from [the obligation of] tithes, as the poor would eat [this] pe'ah in its untithed state [tevel], thinking that it was genuine pe'ah; and gleanings [leket], forgotten sheaves [shikh'chah], and pe'ah are exempt from tithes because they are ownerless.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:2:1.hebrew: גירר עצמות אביו - משום כפרה, ולא קברו בכבוד בדרגש ומטה נאה, ומפני קידוש השם, שיתגנה על רשעו ויוסרו הרשעים:
Rashi on Pesachim 56a:2:1.english: He dragged the bones of his father - For [his] atonement, and he did not bury him with honor on a couch and a handsome bier, and for the sanctification of the [Divine] Name, so that he would be disgraced for his wickedness and the wicked would be chastened.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:2:2.english: He ground the copper snake - Because they were straying after it.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:2:3.hebrew: וגנז ספר רפואות - כדכתיב: "והטוב (והישר) בעיניך עשיתי", ואמרינן בברכות שגנז ספר רפואות, לפי שלא היה לבם נכנע על חולים, אלא מתרפאין מיד:
Rashi on Pesachim 56a:2:3.english: And he suppressed the Book of Cures - As it is written: "And that which is good (and right) in Your eyes I have done," and we say in [Tractate] Berakhot that he suppressed the Book of Cures because their hearts were not humbled over [the] sick, rather they would be healed immediately.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:3:1.hebrew: סתם מי גיחון - כדכתיב (ד"ה ב לב) למען לא יבאו מלכי אשור וימצאו מים לשתות:
Rashi on Pesachim 56a:3:1.english: He sealed the waters of Gihon - As it is written (II Chronicles 32), "so that the kings of Assyria should not come and find water to drink."

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:3:2.english: And they did not concede to him - For he should have trusted in the Holy One, blessed be He, who said (II Kings 19:34), "And I will defend this city to save it."

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:3:3.hebrew: עיבר ניסן בניסן - לאחר שנכנס ניסן, נמלך ועשאו אדר השני, כדכתיב (ד"ה ב ל) "ויועץ המלך חזקיה לעשות פסח בחדש השני וגו'", כי מרבית העם רבים אשר לא הוטהרו עדיין מטומאות שהחזיקו בהן בימי אביו אחז הרשע:
Rashi on Pesachim 56a:3:3.english: He intercalated Nisan during Nisan - After Nisan had begun, he reconsidered and made it the second Adar, as it is written (II Chronicles 30): "And King Hezekiah took counsel to make the Passover in the second month, etc.," because a large majority of the people had not yet been purified from the impurities that they had contracted in the days of his father, the wicked Ahaz.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:3:4.hebrew: ולא הודו לו - כדאמר בסנהדרין ובברכות, החדש הזה וגו' — זה ניסן, ואין אחר ניסן:
Rashi on Pesachim 56a:3:4.english: And they did not concede to him - As [the Gemara] states in Sanhedrin and in Berakhot: "This month, etc." — this is Nisan, and there is no other Nisan.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:4:2.hebrew: ושיכרא דדפנא - שכר של עץ שקורין לו"ר, וגדילין בו פרי שקורין ביי"ש:
Rashi on Pesachim 56a:4:2.english: And laurel beer - Beer [made] from a tree called lor [laurel], and on which grows a fruit called baies [berries].

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:4:3.english: That forty days had not elapsed over it - Since it was ground.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:4:4.hebrew: ושדו ליה לדקלא בליביה - דקל יש לו לב מתוכו, ויש לו מוח לאורכו, כמו שיש לעץ שקורין שנבו"ג ולאגוז. והמשקה הזה מועיל לדקל להתקיים:
Rashi on Pesachim 56a:4:4.english: And they pour it into the palm tree, into its heart [core] - A palm tree has a heart within it, and it has a pith along its length, just as the tree called sambug [elder] and the walnut [tree] have. And this potion is beneficial for the palm tree to survive.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:4:5.english: And any - tree that stands within four cubits of it, for which they do not do this.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:4:7.hebrew: רב אחא בריה דרבא אמר - לאו היינו מרכיבין דמתניתין, אלא מנחי כופרא דוכרא לנוקבתא. מניחין ותוחבין גמזיות רכה בת שנתה שניתוספה באילן בשנה שעברה, וקרי ליה כופרא דיכרא על שם שמכניסין אותו בענף האילן, שקוצץ ענף גדול וסודקו ומשים את זה בתוכו. לשון אחר: כופרא דיכרא — ענף רך של דקל זכר, ומרכיבו בסדק של דקל נקיבה, מפני שדקל נקיבה אינה עושה פירות והזכרים עושין פירות:
Rashi on Pesachim 56a:4:7.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said - That is not [the] "grafting" of our Mishnah; rather, "they place a male shoot (kufra dukhra) into a female [tree]." They place and insert a tender one-year-old shoot that grew on the tree in the past year, and it is called kufra dikhra because they insert it into the branch of the tree — for one cuts a large branch, splits it, and places this inside it. Another explanation: kufra dikhra is a tender branch of a male palm tree, and one grafts it into a slit of a female palm tree, because a female palm tree does not produce fruit, whereas the male [trees] produce fruit.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:5:1.hebrew: וכורכין - כלומר, שהיו מדבקין כל הקרייה כמות שהיא, ולא היו מוסיפין. ואית דגרסי "שהיו אומרים ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו", פי', שהיו אומרים אותו בקול רם:
Rashi on Pesachim 56a:5:1.english: And [they] bundle [Shema] - That is to say, they would join the entire recitation [of Shema] together as it is and would not add [anything]. And some have the reading, "that they would say: Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom" — meaning that they would say it aloud.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:5:2.hebrew: ולא היו מפסיקין - בין ״אחד״ ל״ואהבת״, אע"פ דצריך להאריך ב״אחד״ ולהפסיק בין קבלת מלכות שמים לדברים אחרים, שכל אחד מקבל עליו ואומר ״אחד הוא אלהינו״ בפסוק ראשון, ופסוק שני לשון צוואה היא:
Rashi on Pesachim 56a:5:2.english: And they would not pause - Between "One" [echad] and "And you shall love" [ve'ahavta], even though one must prolong [the pronunciation of] "One" and pause between the acceptance of the kingdom of Heaven and other matters — for everyone accepts upon himself and says, "Our God is One" in the first verse, whereas the second verse is an expression of command.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:5:3.hebrew: ר' יהודה אומר - מפסיקין היו, אלא שלא היו אומרים "ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו":
Rashi on Pesachim 56a:5:3.english: Rabbi Yehuda says - They would pause, but they would not say, "Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom."

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:7:1.hebrew: קץ הימין - שיחזיר ימינו לפניו, שהשיב אחור ימינו מפני אויב:
Rashi on Pesachim 56a:7:1.english: The end of days [lit. the right hand] - [When] He will return His right hand forward, for He had drawn His right hand back from before the enemy.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:7:2.english: Hear, O Israel - They were saying [this] to their father.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:8:1.english: Shall we say it - [Referring] to this [phrase], "Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom," in the recitation of the Shema.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:8:2.english: Drippings of a pot - Arsedura [in Old French] (arsidura: fried and spiced meat).

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:8:3.english: She has suffering - Bodily suffering due to the craving.

Rashi on Pesachim 56a:9:1.hebrew: מפני תרעומת המינין - שלא יהו אומרים עלינו שאנו מוסיפין דבר שאינו הגון בחשאי. ומאן דגרסי שהיו אומרים ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד, מפרש שהיו אומרים אותו בקול רם כשאר הקרייה, וביניהן לא היו מינין:
Rashi on Pesachim 56a:9:1.english: Due to the grievance of the heretics - So that they will not say about us that we are adding something improper in secret. And those who have the reading "that they would say Barukh shem kevod malkhuto le'olam va'ed" ["Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever"] explain that they would say it aloud like the rest of the recitation [of Shema], and among them there were no heretics.

Tosafot on Pesachim 56a:5:1.hebrew: לא היו מפסיקין - בין "שמע ישראל" לשם, דמשמע דאומר לשם שישמע ישראל ויענם:
Tosafot on Pesachim 56a:5:1.english: They would not pause - between "Hear, O Israel" and the [Divine] Name, for it implies that one is saying to God [lit., the Name] that He should hear Israel and answer them.
